course.title: Deep Learning for Computer Vision
course.instructor: Fei-Fei Li, Ehsan Adeli, with Zane Durante and guest lecturers

figureAudit.note: Counts are for the decks of the covered lectures (lecture 1 has two, lectures 2–12 one each). Lecture 1: eight figure-, chart- and table-heavy slides per deck checked at 600 dpi by an independent reader; part 2 clean, part 1 errors on slides 62 and 64, corrected. Lecture 2: fourteen slides checked; errors on slides 8, 33 and 64 and loose detail on 30, 45 and 63, corrected; eight clean. Lecture 3: nineteen slides checked; errors on slides 80, 84 and 99 and small omissions on 13, 86 and 122, corrected; the absence of optimizer paths on slides 61, 70, 75 and 109 confirmed. Lecture 4: twenty-three slides checked by two readers, who rendered at 150–200 dpi rather than the 600 asked for (crops at 400–600 dpi on slides 11, 53 and 116); errors on slides 11, 25 and 26 and small omissions on 41, 96, 116 and 134, corrected; slide 143's matrices confirmed again on the 1400px render of slide 150; no figure on slide 50 and no optimizer paths on slide 10 confirmed. Lecture 5: twenty-four slides checked by two readers, again at about 200 dpi effective (600 dpi renders downscaled by the viewer), with 600 dpi crops of slides 127, 129 and 133; errors on slides 4, 22, 24 and 81 and small fixes on 35, 38, 80, 108 and 136, corrected; slide 6's matrices, slide 62's K_w x K_h order, slide 101's swapped labels, slide 124's wording, slide 127's numbers and slide 129's minus signs confirmed; slides 81 and 101 checked again on their 1400px renders, which corrected one cell position on 81. Lecture 6: twenty-four slides checked by two readers, who rendered at 600 dpi but read most pages downscaled (about 110–130 dpi), with crops of slides 35, 41 and 73 at 300 dpi and 57, 61, 63 and 65 at 600 dpi; corrections on slides 35 (each VGG stack draws two 3x3 conv, 256 boxes), 41, 63, 73, 75, 78, 79 and 95; slide 11's "per batch" annotation, slide 57's "3x3 conv, 64" label and every histogram value on slides 61, 63 and 65 confirmed; slide 35 checked again on its 1400px render. Lecture 7: twenty-seven slides checked by two readers from crops of 600 dpi renders (eight from page views at about 150 dpi); corrections on slides 7, 58, 61, 88 (the captioning CNN draws 10 conv layers, not 8) and 131; every vector on slides 61–66, slide 67's code listing, slide 111's equation, slide 116's code and slide 129's labels confirmed; slides 65 and 66 checked again on their 1400px renders. Lecture 8: thirty-three slides checked by two readers from crops of 600 dpi renders (slide 63 from a page view only); corrections on slides 20 (arrows around s0 and the '+'), 26 and 27 (the extent of the coloured boxes) and 100–101 (a line on the photograph that is not there; the patch contents), small additions on 81, 93, 109 and 112; every equation checked agreed. One report contradicted itself on which way up the attention grids are drawn; the text layer settled it (key 1's row on top on slides 43–61, at the bottom in the pasted figure on slides 4 and 121). Slides 19, 20, 27 and 61 checked again on 1400px renders. Lecture 9: thirty-seven slides checked by two readers from 600 dpi renders, with crops of every value on fourteen of them and half-page crops on most of the rest (ten slides, among them the Mask R-CNN head, the RoI shapes and the timing charts, from whole-page views only); corrections on slides 3 (four encoder and four decoder bars), 43 and 64 (two high-resolution slabs, not three), 60-61 (three bars per U-Net level), 96, 97 and 107 (which DETR predictions are matched to 'no object'), and an arithmetic error in the transcriber's editorial note on 127; the repeated x2 on 3, slide 43's 'Low-res' label, every grid on 45, 46, 152 and 176 and the bar values on 165 and 169 confirmed; slides 60 and 165 checked again on their 1400px renders. Lecture 10: thirty-nine slides checked by two readers from crops of 600 dpi renders, with the printed text, the tables and the chart values checked against the PDF's text layer; corrections on slides 28, 37, 38 (six labels per frame, red bars on lower predictions), 43, 47 (the temporal stream's conv2 prints no 'norm.'), 85 (17 frames, not 15) and 99, small additions on 36, 70, 76, 77 and 81; slide 39's fifth bar is in the text layer only; slides 85 and 76 checked again on their 1400px renders. Lecture 11: forty-three slides checked by two readers, one from 600 dpi crops throughout (the code listings character by character, every table cell and every pipeline-schedule cell), the other from 600 dpi crops on the hardware slides, 400 dpi crops on 61–63 and 200–250 dpi views elsewhere, with the checkpointing counters also read from the text layer; corrections on slides 17 (no line at Mar-23; the dates of every point), 24, 27, 56, 61 (GPU 1 holds W_2) and 62, small additions on 10, 12, 139 (block labels in its text layer that are not visible), 146 and 147; the parent's checks of the 1400px renders of 61 and 106 restored the plain 'dL/dW_i' of slides 55–58's list text. Lecture 12: forty-three slides checked by two readers, both from 600 dpi crops throughout; corrections on slides 22 (where the curves cross), 39 (three curves at the first layers), 59, 89 (the code boxes), 91 and 100 from the first, and on 8, 16 (the GPT-4 abstract is legible; the robot photo), 24, 26, 37, 45, 53 (exact patch and token counts), 101 (a 7 x 7 grid), 106, 115 and 116 from the second; every table cell and both code listings agreed; slide 31's unbalanced bracket confirmed; the parent's checks of the 1400px renders of 39 and 53 agreed.

caveats: Covers lectures 1-12 of 18 only; nothing on lectures 13-18.

Lecture 1 has two slide decks, each numbered from 1; cite as 'part 1, slide N' / 'part 2, slide N'. Part 2's printed numbers skip 4, 5 and 45, lecture 2's skip 32 and 49, lecture 3's skip 10, 11, 12 and 29, and lecture 4's skip 2, 47, 112, 113 and 114, so printed numbers run ahead of PDF page numbers. Lecture 5's 141 and lecture 6's 97 printed numbers match their PDF pages. Lecture 7's skip 19, 20, 52, 53, 71, 72, 73, 100 and 103, and its page 118 prints no number (slide 127). Lecture 8's 122, lecture 9's 178 and lecture 10's 103 printed numbers match their PDF pages; lecture 10's pages 5, 6, 88-91, 93-95 and 100 print no number, and their labels follow from their neighbours; lecture 11's 148 printed numbers match its PDF pages. Lecture 12's skip 112 and 113, so its slides 114-117 are PDF pages 112-115.
Lecture 1's logistics slides (part 2, slides 33-48 and 50) were not presented in the recording; wiki/course-logistics.md is sourced to the slides as posted on April 1, 2025.

Lecture 2's recording skips its administrative slides (2-4) and ends mid-sentence at 1:06:37, before the multiclass SVM loss (a reading assignment, slides 85-100) and softmax vs. SVM (slides 101-104); those are sourced to the slides alone, and their quiz questions have no printed answers.

Lecture 3's recording skips its administrative slides (2-4) and ends at 1:08:25 in the look ahead to neural networks; slides 100-101 and the appendix of 'Slides from Previous Years' (slides 102-123: Nesterov momentum, AdaGrad, L-BFGS, softmax vs. SVM) are sourced to the slides alone.

Lecture 4's recording skips its administrative slides (3-4) and the 'Today: Deep Learning' examples (slides 12-21: DALL-E 2 and 3, GPT-4, Segment Anything, Sora); those are sourced to the slides alone. It covers the matrix-multiply example (slides 143-150) only in outline.

Lecture 5's recording skips its administrative slides (2-3) and its appendix of 'Slides from Previous Years' (slides 109-141: older convolution and pooling summaries, 1x1 convolutions, the neuron view, the ConvNetJS demo, the deep-learning recipe and a history from the Mark I Perceptron to the Neocognitron); those are sourced to the slides alone. The appendix uses K for the number of filters and F for the filter size, where the lecture uses K for the kernel size.

Lecture 6's recording skips only its course-logistics slide (2), which is sourced to the slide alone; it adds spoken answers on LoRA and on ResNet's paired convolutions (1:04:40-1:06:59) that no slide shows.

Lecture 7's recording skips only its course-logistics slide (2), which is sourced to the slide alone. Several spoken answers go beyond the slides (chunked backpropagation, embedding layers, greedy decoding and beam search); one, on truncated backpropagation through time (31:48-35:36), describes carrying a gradient across chunk boundaries, which the slides do not draw, and the wiki says so. The interpretable-cell colour code (red -1, blue 1) is spoken, not printed.

Lecture 8's recording skips its administrative slide (2) and does not walk through four parts of the deck, which are sourced to the slides alone: the matrix-shape and memory slides (68-78, summarised in a sentence), the GPT-2 and GPT-3 sizes (94-95), transformer language models (96-99, one sentence) and 'Tweaking Transformers' (110-120: pre-norm, RMSNorm, SwiGLU, mixture of experts), left 'as extra reading' (lecture 9 walks through the same slides, its 20-29). The lecturer is not named in the recording or on the deck.

Lecture 9's recording skips its administrative slide (2) and the deck's 'Additional Reading Material' (slides 150-178: convolution and transposed convolution as matrix multiplication, RoI Pool and RoI Align, the R-CNN timing charts, Faster R-CNN's four losses and two stages, detection trade-offs, guided backpropagation), which are sourced to the slides alone. The per-pixel segmentation loss and the answers about DETR's object queries are spoken only. The lecturer is not named in the recording or on the deck.

Lecture 10 is a guest lecture by Ruohan Gao. Its recording covers the deck up to slide 102 (slide 103, 'Next time', is not reached); the McGurk slides (89-91) are never mentioned and the 'Apply Eye Makeup' visualization (82-83) is not spoken, so both are sourced to the slides alone. Several slides are stills of embedded videos (5, 6, 43, 88-91, 93-96): the PDF holds one frame each, and what the videos showed is known only where the lecturer describes it (the point-light display of slide 43). The toy size and receptive-field tables (24-31) and the C3D cost table (41) are walked through in words; their values come from the slides.

Lecture 11's lecturer is not named in the recording or on the deck. Its recording skips the administrative slide (2: midterm review session Friday 5/9, in-class midterm Tuesday 5/13) and does not reach slide 148 ('Next time'). After MFU the lecturer says the remaining slides can be checked offline, so context, pipeline and tensor parallelism (slides 114-144) get a brief spoken tour and their details are sourced to the slides. Spoken only: binning (132 of 144 SMs), the 20x slowdown of a model left in 32-bit, training-run lengths, cluster size and cooling, asynchronous SGD, DistributedDataParallel and CUDA, MFU above 50% on A100s.

Lecture 12's lecturer is not named in the recording or on the deck. Its recording opens with a recap, skips the administrative slide (2: midterm Tuesday 5/13 during lecture time, review section Friday 5/9 at 12:30 pm, proposal feedback on Gradescope), and stops after MoCo v2 (slide 93). Contrastive predictive coding, MoCo v3, DINO, DINOv2, the summary of contrastive learning (slides 94-111) and the appendix (slides 114-117: CPC on images, Dense Object Net) are sourced to the slides alone. Slides 48-51 (video colourisation and tracking, credited to a Google AI blog post) hold one still per panel; whether they played as animations is not knowable from the PDF.

Lecture 3's optimizer-comparison slides (60, 61's gradient-noise panel, 70, 75, 109) were animations: the PDF shows only the loss surface and legend, so the optimizers' paths are known only from the lecturer's spoken description. Lecture 4's recap slide 10 and lecture 5's recap slide 8 repeat one of these frames.

Lecture 2's deck prints two arithmetic slips in worked examples (slide 60's ship score omits the bias; slide 101's 0.452 is a base-10 log); both are kept as printed and noted. Lecture 3 repeats the slide 101 example as its slide 119, with the same base-10 value, and its slide 34 prints 0.1555 as '15.5%'. Lecture 4's slide 53 prints a plus where a minus belongs in its expanded hinge term, and its matrix-multiply example (slides 143-150) prints an output y that is not the product of its x and w (x times w is [[-1, -1, 2, 6], [5, 2, 11, 7]]); both kept as printed and noted. Lecture 5's deck has four: slide 6 repeats lecture 2's bias-less ship score (61.95 for 60.75), slide 101 swaps its cube labels (the input is 64 x 224 x 224, the output 64 x 112 x 112), slide 124 says 'Conv layer needs 2 hyperparameters' under the heading 'Pooling layer: summary', and slide 129 prints the softmax loss with minus signs in both exponents. Lecture 6's deck has four oddities, none in its arithmetic, each kept as printed and noted: slide 11's LayerNorm annotation says 'Statistics calculated per batch' for N x 1 per-sample statistics; slide 35's VGG16 and VGG19 stacks draw 15 and 17 weight layers (two '3x3 conv, 256' boxes each); slide 57 labels ResNet's last stage '3x3 conv, 64' where slides 53-56 print 512; slides 78-79 point to 'Lecture 13' for visualization, which is lecture 9 in Spring 2025. Lecture 7's deck has six, each kept as printed and noted: slide 65's sampling softmax is wrong in its first two columns (scores (1.0, 2.2, -3.0, 4.1) and (0.5, 0.3, -1.0, 1.2) give about (.04, .13, .00, .84) and (.25, .20, .06, .50), not the printed (.03, .84, .00, .13) and (.25, .20, .50, .05)), which the lecturer acknowledges at 38:42 and 43:21; slide 66's matrix ends rows 2 and 3 in w14; slide 106 writes W_xh and then W_hx; slide 110's chain has a lowercase t where it means T; slide 116's clipping code computes the squared norm and calls it the norm; slide 129 repeats lecture 6's '3x3 conv, 64' label. Lecture 8's deck has six, each kept as printed and noted: slide 62's faded output line reads Y = AX for Y = AV (repeated on 63); the multi-head slides (66-78) keep the single-head scale sqrt(D_Q), where each head's query dimension is D_H; slide 77's '1.192 TB' for 64 heads of 100K x 100K attention weights mixes units (at 2 bytes a weight it is 1,192 GiB, or 1.28 TB); slide 82 prints O(N) memory for self-attention, which slide 78 gives only with Flash Attention; slide 111 prints 'identify function'; slide 113's RMSNorm averages over N entries of a vector of shape D. Lecture 9's deck has six, each kept as printed and noted: slide 3's encoder labels its inputs x0, x1, x2, x2; slides 4, 21 and 23 repeat lecture 8's O(N) memory, 'identify function' and RMSNorm N-vs-D slips; slide 43 labels the low-resolution stage 'D3 x H/4 x W/4', the same as the medium-resolution stages (repeated on 44 and 59); slide 127 reprints lecture 2's bias-less ship score (61.95 for 60.75). Lecture 10's deck has four, each kept as printed and noted: slide 30 prints the 3D CNN's pooled output as '24 x 1 x 1', a dimension short (24 x 1 x 1 x 1); slides 35-37 label the 3D filter 'Slide over x and y' although it also slides over time; slide 41's column headed 'MFLOPs' holds GFLOPs (it sums to 39.5), and its fully connected rows (0.51, 0.45, 0.05) do not recompute from the layer sizes (about 0.019 and 0.017 for FC6 and FC7); slide 75 says to copy the kernel 'K_t times in space' where the copies go along time. Lecture 11's deck has eight, each kept as printed and noted: slide 25's '1.875 PB' is 24,576 x 80 GB in binary units (about 1.97 PB decimal); slides 46-64 are titled 'FSPD' and cite 'Rajbhandrari et al'; slide 68 lists 'Adam β1, β1' where slide 44 has 'β1, β2'; slide 69's '63GB' is binary (67.6 GB decimal) and its Llama3-405B sequence length 4096 differs from the 8192 of slides 125 and 146; slide 98's checkpointing counter prints 'Current Memory: 2' with one box drawn, and slides 100-101 keep the counter (14 / 2 / 2) while drawing all eight boxes; slide 112's Llama3-405B row of 400 TFLOPs/GPU prints 41% MFU, where 400 / 989.4 is 40.4% (repeated on 113 and 146); slide 138 says to shard the first layer 'over row' and the second 'over column', the opposite of its drawing (column blocks, then row blocks) and of the lecturer's words; slides 139-143 label Z '[DxD]' where Z = YU is N x D. Lecture 12's deck has two, each kept as printed and noted: slide 31's adversarial loss has unbalanced brackets (the expectation's '[' closes after log(D(x)), and a second ']' follows the last term); slide 81 draws a row of 10 vectors (2N = 10) beside an affinity matrix of 6 x 6 cells, both labelled 2N. Its tables, reproduced from different papers, disagree on the same rows (supervised ImageNet 78.9/79.9 on slide 23 against 78.2% on 27 and 33; the context encoder's segmentation 29.7 against 30.0%).

Verbatim auto-captions are not published; the transcripts are copy-edits with every restoration listed in their headers, seven passages marked unclear in lecture 1, five in lecture 2, three in lecture 3, one in lecture 4, five in lecture 5, three in lecture 6, three in lecture 7, six in lecture 8, ten in lecture 9, 39 in lecture 10 (a guest lecture whose captions are heavily garbled in places) five in lecture 11 and nine in lecture 12.
